doc.title: Steve Wilson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 25, 2002

chapter: Richmond and arriving in New York
title: Peter Leitch's duo gig and learning tunes by roots
summary: Learning obscure tunes for Peter Leitch and his method of learning root movement, chords, then melody.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: It’s impossible. As a matter of fact I occasionally play with a great guitarist named Peter Leitch. He has a regular Sunday night gig in New York at a place called Walker’s. Just a duo. And every week he has somebody different. And I do the gig like every couple of months and it’s good for that because Peter knows a million tunes in any key, and he knows these obscure tunes that nobody knows, all of these different Broadway tunes. So just last week I played with him again and I remember the time before that his wife Sylvia had asked me if I knew one of the tunes from “Kismet,” “Stranger in Paradise.” So I went out and I bought the record and I learned it. Now I learned it in the original key which was G flat. And of course when I got on the gig, Peter is playing it in F. Okay, here we go. But that’s part of the music.

Right. I sometimes feel sorry for the bass players at sessions. For one thing they have to play forever, plus it seems to me as a horn player you can kind of — well you don’t have to know the roots all the time. You can negotiate with your ear somewhat. But the bass player, I hope he knows the changes.

Yeah. Well you know ironically that’s what I’m listening for is roots most of the time. And when I’m learning tunes I do it in two ways. I go to the piano and learn what the root movement is, I learn the chords and then the melody. So that way I can correlate the melody with the root movement. So whenever I’m caught in a situation where I’m not very familiar I find that those bookends, the outline, helps me a lot. Because if I can’t
hear one or the other I’m really lost. I’m like okay well I’m just out there. But it’s saved me more than a few times.
